newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER TO STAY UNTIL END OF THE CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER TO STAY UNTIL END OF THE CENTURY.

text.p: Michael Schumacher has agreed to stay with Ferrari until the end of the 1999 Formula One season, the Italian company said in a statement on Tuesday.

Schumacher, world champion in 1994 and 1995, helped his new team to second place in the constructors' championship this season. He also won three races and finished third in the drivers' championship.
"Michael is not just the best driver in the world. He is also a man who knows how to work with a team and for a team," Ferrari president Luca di Montezemolo said.

Schumacher's original contract was due to expire at the end of the 1997 season, but Ferrari officials indicated last month they wanted the German driver to stay longer as they bid to win their first drivers' title since 1979.

"I am sure that in the next three years we will reap the fruits of this great common effort and we will give our supporters -- shareholders, sponsors and fans -- the satisfaction they deserve," di Montezemolo said in a statement.
Ferrari also said Briton Eddie Irvine would carry on as the team's co-driver until the end of next year and added his contract would include an option covering the 1998 season.
The brief statement from the group's northern Italian headquarters of Maranello gave no financial details of either deal.
The 27-year-old Schumacher's arrival in the Ferrari camp from Benetton raised Italian hopes early in the season, culminating in the German driver's victory at the Spanish Grand Prix in June.

The team suffered three successive double failures mid-season when both Schumacher and Irvine were forced to quit races after a string of unrelated engine problems, although Schumacher won both the Belgian and Italian Grand Prix towards the close of the season.
Buoyed by these successes, di Montezemolo had said last month he had set his sights on the title in 1997 or 1998, preferably in 1997.
He added that Schumacher had been signed at just the right moment for the team. "If we had signed him a year before it maybe would have been a mistake. A waste."
Ferrari have not produced a champion driver since South African Jody Scheckter in 1979 and have not won the constructors' championship since 1983.
The son of a provincial bricklayer, Schumacher dedicated himself to motor racing at an early age and joined the Formula One circuit in 1991.
